explanation: Jesus corresponds to Muhammad: In Christianity, Jesus is the savior and Son of God, and is the core of Christian faith. In Islam, Muhammad is the last prophet and the core of Islamic faith. Both are important figures and centers of faith in their respective religions.

Palestine corresponds to the Arabian Peninsula: Christianity originated in the region of Palestine, while Islam originated in the Arabian Peninsula. Both are the birthplaces of their respective religions.

The Bible corresponds to the Quran: The Bible is the classic of Christianity, containing the teachings and beliefs of Christianity. The Quran is the classic of Islam, containing the teachings and beliefs of Islam. Both are the classics and sources of doctrine for their respective religions.

background.source: Christianity is a major world religion that originated in Palestine in the 1st century AD. It was founded on the life and teachings of Jesus of Nazareth, who was considered to be the Son of God by his followers. Today, Christianity is the world's largest religion, with over 2.4 billion followers from all around the world. The Bible, comprising both the Old Testament and the New Testament, is the primary text of the religion and contains the teachings of Jesus and his followers. The religion has gone through numerous schisms and developments throughout its history, resulting in a variety of denominations and beliefs. Despite this, the core belief among all Christians is that Jesus died on the cross for the salvation of humanity and rose again on the third day. While Christianity began in the Middle East, it has since spread throughout the world, with significant numbers of Christians now residing in Africa and Asia. However, despite its widespread popularity, Christians continue to be persecuted in many parts of the world, particularly in the Middle East, North Africa, East Asia, and South Asia.
background.target: Islam is a popular Abrahamic monotheistic religion that follows the teachings of the Quran and the prophet Muhammad. Its followers, called Muslims, number around 1.9 billion globally and are the second-largest religious population after Christians. The religion centers around a belief that there is only one God, and that Muhammad is the main and final prophet of Islam. Muslims take the Quran to be the word of God, and the teachings and examples of Muhammad are considered constitutional models for followers. The Islamic faith has five pillars – the shahada or Islamic oath and creed, daily prayers, almsgiving, fasting, and the annual pilgrimage to Mecca. Sharia, the Islamic law, influences many aspects of life – from social and economic issues to the environment. Islamic festivals such as Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha are also of great significance to the followers. With its origin in Mecca in the 7th Century, Islam has grown gradually and now has a sizable presence in many parts of the world, and comprises of two major denominations, Sunni Islam and Shia Islam.
